findings.issue: expl_en explains a completely different sentence (君が怒るのももっともだ: の-nominalization, もっともだ, も vs は) — copy-paste error. It matches nothing in this sentence and contradicts expl_pt, which correctly explains the quotative と + しかった structure.
findings.current: Same construction: 君が怒る ('you getting angry') nominalized by の, predicate もっともだ ('it's natural'). The difference is も instead of は...
findings.suggested: 彼は topic; 注意が足りない ('not careful enough') is an inner clause quoted by と (content of the scolding); 息子をしかった 'scolded his son': を object, た past.

findings.issue: 何時 here is read なんじ ('what o'clock'): it takes に and the translations say 'what time / a que horas'. いつに is unnatural Japanese (いつ does not normally take に), so the kana teaches a wrong reading.
findings.current: がっこうわいつにおわるの?
findings.suggested: がっこうわなんじにおわるの?

findings.issue: Reading of 何時 in context is なんじ (clock time, followed by に and glossed 'at what time'); いつ is the wrong reading here.
Romaji follows the wrong いつ reading; with the correct reading なんじ it should be nanji.
The explanation states the reading of 何時 as いつ; in this sentence (何時に + 'what time') it is なんじ. Teaches a false reading fact.
findings.current: 何時 (いつ, 'at what time') is the interrogative word, followed by に to mark the moment.
findings.suggested: 何時 (なんじ, 'at what time') is the interrogative word, followed by に to mark the moment.

findings.issue: Same wrong reading claim as expl_en: 何時 here is なんじ, not いつ.
findings.current: 何時 (いつ, 'a que horas') é a palavra interrogativa, seguida de に para marcar o momento.
findings.suggested: 何時 (なんじ, 'a que horas') é a palavra interrogativa, seguida de に para marcar o momento.

findings.issue: 何してる is read なにしてる in standard Japanese (何 is なに before する; なん appears before だ/で/と/counters). なんしてる is dialectal/nonstandard and wrong as the taught reading.
findings.current: がっこうがおわってからなんしてる?
findings.suggested: がっこうがおわってからなにしてる?

findings.issue: Reading of 何 before してる is なに in standard Japanese, not なん.
Romaji follows the wrong なん reading; standard reading is nani shiteru.

In わけがない, ない follows the subject particle が (わけ + が + ない), so it is the i-adjective ない 'to not exist' acting as the predicate — not the verbal negation auxiliary, which attaches to verb stems (as in 足りない). The role teaches a false analysis.
With the correct in-context reading なんじ, the added sense 'when' (the いつ reading) does not apply; 何時(なんじ)に asks specifically for clock time.
Same as the en gloss: 'quando' belongs to the いつ reading, not to なんじに in this sentence.
